GitLab has two types of customer escalations: Account Escalation and Support Ticket Attention Requests (STAR).
An Account Escalation at GitLab can be opened by anyone in the company.
Account Escalations at GitLab should not be used to raise the priority of a single support ticket.
Support Ticket Attention Requests (STAR) are used when an open support ticket is moving too slowly or needs a priority increase.
Account Escalations at GitLab focus on issues such as delays across multiple tickets or systemic support concerns.

A success plan at GitLab is the roadmap for achieving a customer's business objectives using the platform.
A success plan serves as the foundation of every Customer Success Manager (CSM) engagement.
The three core components of a success plan are Objective, Initiative, and Verifiable Outcome (VO).
An Objective is defined by a clear goal, measurable success criteria, owners, and a timeline.
A Verifiable Outcome (VO) must be SMART, formally tracked, customer-validated, and reported quarterly.
